The Rhinosaur are units from the Monolith official scenario map in Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne and is seen as the hero for this race. __NOTOC__ Rin'ji is forest troll kept prisoner in a cage inside Quel'Danil Lodge in the Hinterlands. Whilst his tribe, Witherbark was an enemy of the Horde, Rin'ji made a personal deal with members of the Horde in which in return for helping him escape from the high elves, he would give them a rare tablet of Witherbark history. After being escorted, he run towards Shadra'Alor. In the game, Rin'ji was not only friendly to Horde members, but was also flagged as a Horde member himself. He has been missing since the Cataclysm, presumably having returned to his village.

The Ring of Trials, also called the Nagrand Arena, is an arena located in Nagrand, southeast of Garadar. It was, along with the Circle of Blood Arena, added in The Burning Crusade and thus among the first arenas added to the game. Unlike most arenas, Ring of Trials can be accessed in the outdoor world in addition to its instanced version, serving as a PvA arena. Lorewise, it used to be an ancient orcish proving ground, although before the destruction of Draenor it was built using imperial ogre architecture.

The Ring of the Law is located inside Blackrock Depths. It is accessed through the Halls of the Law just beyond the Detention Block. When a player stands on the mesh circle at the center of this area, it starts the Ring of Law boss event. The entrance to the ring is closed, and High Justice Grimstone appears in the ring. This dark iron dwarf is flagged red, but cannot be attacked; his purpose is to explain what is about to happen. Once the players are victorious in the ring, the ring's entrance reopens, and a second gate also opens, leading to the ring's upper levels and the rest of the instance. The Ring of Balance is a training arena used by the students Tian Monastery. The ring is located in the southwestern portion of the monastery, which itself can be found in north-central Jade Forest. Instructor Xann watches over the arena. During the Burning Legion's third invasion, the area was used by Hozen Students to train. Later, it was attacked by demons.

The Ring of Inner Focus, also know as the Rumpus Pit, is a training arena used by the students at Tian Monastery. The ring is located in the northwestern corner of the monastery, which itself can be found in north-central Jade Forest. Instructor Myang watches over the arena. The ring was attacked by the Burning Legion.

The Ring of Conquest is a sub-zone in western Ashran, on . A heavily controlled area filled with toughened elite ogres, the Ring of Conquest is intended to offer a stiffer challenge than the other secondary areas. The denizens of the area are substantial elites, hardened brawlers and stone-based elementalists. The area appears to be controlled by the Ashmaul. Not for the faint hearted, the area is preceded by a signpost placed by Harrison Jones, which states "This area has been flagged as too dangerous for casual explorers. Proceed with extreme caution."

Rikati is a vulpera quest giver and wasp farmer located at the Four Stingers in Vol'dun. He specializes in extracting the bilewing wasps' "honey" (in other words, venom) from their stingers and selling it. He is friends with Rhan'ka; even though Rikati considers the troll to be "crazier than a bag of ranishu" and has no idea what Rhan'ka does with all of the honey he buys, he is still Rikati's best customer. After Rhan'ka's Goldtusk Inn is ransacked by the Sandfury, he rides by the Four Stingers and tells Rikati to hide his honey from the Sandfury bandits. Rhan'ka also asks adventurers to visit Rikati and get some bottles of his honey, "de best honey in all of Vol'dun", to add some sweetness

The Rikkitun sprites are a tribe dwell in and around Rikkitun Village in the Dread Wastes. They are protected from the mantid due to an agreement made many millennia ago. There are forces from which they are not safe, however. The kyparite worms beneath the ground to the west of Rikkitun will haunt, chase and even eat sprites, and the mistlurkers eat sprites by the handful. The pact seems to involve the sprites overseeing Kypari tree reproductive cycle.

A risen centaur warrior is a centaur that has risen in undeath into a skeletal creature. Khan Krenka became a risen centaur in undeath.

Rituals are spells that require more than one participant (usually 3 participants), similar to Meeting Stones. They usually involve the casting player channeling a spell, which creates a portal nearby. Friendly players must click on the portal to join in the ritual, with the spell completing once a sufficient number of players are participating. Current rituals include: *Warlock's Ritual of Summoning -- Summon a non-present party member to the warlock's location.
Risen Vrykul Ancestors are vrykul skeletons found at the ancient burial ground of Shield Hill in the Howling Fjord.
Risen Crypt Lords are crypt lords located at the Sands of Nasam in the Borean Tundra.
Riplash Siren is a deceased naga found at the northern half of the Riplash Ruins in the Borean Tundra. She was presumably killed by the vrykul who now inhabit the area.
Riplash Myrmidons are naga located in Riplash Ruins in the Borean Tundra.
Riplash Sorceresses are deceased naga located in the Shrine of Scales in the Borean Tundra.
Risen Wintergarde Mages are skeletal mages located in the Carrion Fields in the Dragonblight.
Risen Wintergarde Defenders are skeletons located in the Wintergarde Mine in the Dragonblight.

Risen Drudges are ghouls wandering around in Acherus: The Ebon Hold in the Eastern Plaguelands. They are completely loyal to the Ebon Blade.
The Rise of Suffering is a ledge at the eastern end of Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate in Icecrown.

Risen Drakkari Handlers were Drakkari ice trolls in charge of watching over the raptors in Drak'Tharon Keep. They have been killed and raised as scourge trolls by Scourge necromancers. They ride Drakkari Raptor Mounts.

Risen Zombies are level 78-80 zombies found during the Culling of Stratholme. They are also present during The Deaths of Chromie.

The Riplash are a group of naga found at Riplash Ruins and Riplash Strand in the Borean Tundra. At some point after the Great Sundering, the Riplash naga took the Riplash Ruins over and replaced the statue of Elune inside its temple with one of Queen Azshara. 500 years ago, Raj Naz'jan was the emperor of the Riplash naga, when the kraken Leviroth was imprisoned in the waters below the ruins by Azshara herself. She then blessed his trident so it would slay the beast should it ever escape. They were using massive generators to melt the surrounding glaciers and ice caps, threatening to flood the entire region.
